candidates.why: remove_NOD_item (called at 1390/1394) frees _obj->texts[i] at 1360 and memmove-shifts texts[i+1..] down at 1363, decrementing numitems at 1366. The enclosing for-loop at 1397 then does i++ and re-reads _obj->texts[i] at 1388/1393 for the next iteration; the shifted-in element is now at index i and the loop bound uses the mutated numitems, so the array state read after the free/shift is inconsistent with the loop index. Suspicious index/array desync after free.

remove_NOD_item frees _obj->itemhandles[i] at 1362 (when !is_global) then memmove-shifts itemhandles[i+1..] at 1364. If the same non-global Dwg_Object_Ref* is also referenced by another object's field (shared ref), freeing it here leaves that other reference dangling. Cross-object aliasing of non-global refs is not ruled out by the code.

find_section_info_type (1707-1717) returns &dwg->header.section_info[i]. At 2843-2844 section_info is realloc'd (old block freed). Callers at 2943/2971/2995/3069 obtain info via find_section_info_type; if any such pointer is held across the realloc at 2844 it becomes dangling. Suspicious realloc-invalidation of returned interior pointer.

copy_R2004_section calls bit_chain_alloc(dat) at 1422 which reallocs dat->chain (bits.c:3015), then memcpy from decomp at 1425. In the current caller (3129) decomp is sec_dat[type].chain (distinct from dat), so no aliasing today, but the function signature does not forbid decomp aliasing dat->chain; if it ever did, the realloc at 1422 would free the source before the memcpy at 1425. Also bit_chain_alloc only grows by CHAIN_BLOCK (1024) once, so a large decomp_data_size can overflow the buffer at 1425.
